title: cost-econ-hosting-alignment-paloma-dataworks
summary: Intro discovery to map Paloma's per-token constraints and deployment preferences; key tradeoffs discussed: batching vs latency, hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC), KV cache benefits, SOC2/KMS requirements. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot cost simulation and provide detailed pilot scope + security docs.
next_steps: Redwood to send pilot cost spreadsheet and sample per-token scenarios (Ethan)
Paloma to share expected QPS, average prompt/response token lengths, and PII/data residency constraints (Sara)
Schedule pilot kickoff next Wednesday 12/17 10am PT (Maya)
Redwood to attach SOC2 summary, KMS integration notes, and example VPC diagram
action_items: Ethan Ruiz | build per-token pilot simulation (3 scenarios: hosted baseline, dedicated reserved pool, private VPC with on-prem quantized model) | 2027-12-17
Maya Thompson | schedule kickoff and send calendar invite + pricing sheet | 2027-12-13
Sara Lin | provide traffic profile: 7-day sample CSV, token distribution, 99th percentile latency target | 2027-12-15
Tomás Ortega | confirm network constraints and whether HSM/KMS is required in-region | 2027-12-16
Leah Park | approve pilot budget ceiling ($8k) or confirm flexibility | 2027-12-14
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-12-10 15:00 UTC, Duration: ~62 minutes, Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Sara (Paloma ML), Tomas (Platform), Leah (CFO)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you carving out time. quick agenda, map your constraints on cost per inference, latency SLOs, and security residency so we can scope a pilot.
[00:17] Sara: yeah thanks, hi. uh we teamed up to look at inference costs for our customer-facing summarization feature. main ask is keep per-interaction cost under, sort of, an equivalent of $0.015 per call on average.
[00:29] Leah: hi all, i'm mostly here for the budget constraints — we have a tight runway and need to validate numbers before commit.
[00:37] Ethan: got it, thanks. when you say per-call, can you unpack tokens? like prompt length, response length, are you using streaming?
[00:45] Sara: typical prompt is 250 tokens, response target about 300 tokens, sometimes up to 800 for long docs. streaming would be nice but not mandatory.
[01:02] Tomás: and QPS today is tiny — about 3 rps peak, but we expect bursts during business hours to ~40 rps; spiky.
[01:12] Maya: good — that pattern matters a lot for batching economics. just to surface quickly, we can model three pathways: hosted (our API), dedicated reserved capacity, or private VPC/on-prem. each has different fixed and variable cost profiles.
[01:27] Sara: we tried another provider and they were cheaper on paper but performance was poor; latency spiked. also we need SOC2, and some data must stay in EU region.
[01:38] Maya: noted. we have SOC2 and EU regions, and private deployment can be done with customer-managed VPC or on-prem if required.
[01:47] Ethan: diving into the economics — per-token pricing matters but so do batching and KV cache. for your workload: shortish prompts and medium responses, we expect caching prefixes to be effective for repeated document headers, and batching will help during bursts.
[02:02] Sara: can you explain KV cache again? earlier calls had the SE say K-V cache, i think?
[02:08] Ethan: yeah, KV cache — key-value attention cache for autoregressive models. it saves the hidden states for prefixes so repeated parts don't get recomputed. in practice it reduces per-token GPU work for repeated prompts by up to 30-60% depending on prefix reuse.
[02:25] Tomás: is that compatible with private on-prem quantized models? we have a 16GB GPU fleet on-prem.
[02:31] Ethan: yes, but for quantized paths there are nuances — some quant kernels are less friendly to dynamic KV eviction and batching. we can profile.
[02:41] Leah: so what are the rough numbers? hosted per-token vs dedicated?
[02:45] Maya: ballpark: hosted API variable charge could look like $0.0008–$0.0015 per input token and similar for output depending on model. dedicated amortizes GPU cost — could be lower per-token if you have steady high utilization, e.g., amortized down to $0.0005–$0.0009 per token for heavy sustained load, but you pay committed monthly. private/on-prem removes per-token variable charges but you absorb infra ops and model maintenance.
[03:11] Sara: hmm our usage is spiky though, committed reserved looks risky. we like burst capacity.
[03:17] Ethan: that's where hybrid reserved+burst comes in — Redwood Dedicated supports reserved pools plus burst to hosted; you can set routing policies to prefer reserved for critical traffic and fall back to hosted.
[03:28] Tomás: latency — we need 95th percentile < 450ms for most flows. does batching break that?
[03:35] Ethan: depends on your batching window. continuous batching can yield throughput wins with small impact on p95 if you set target latency SLOs per route. we can set small batching deadlines 10–25ms to boost throughput with minimal impact. but at very low QPS batching gains are limited.
[03:53] Sara: what about quantization? can we get cost down further?
[03:56] Ethan: yes, 8-bit or 4-bit quantized models reduce memory and inference costs; depending on model and workload quality delta is often acceptable. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles by workload and can recommend when to use them.
[04:12] Leah: legal/security: we need KMS, audit logs, SAML SSO, and the ability to disable data retention for certain routes. is that supported?
[04:21] Maya: yes — KMS integration, full audit logs in Redwood Console, RBAC, SAML/SSO. retention policies can be per-route or tenant-level; optional disable for sensitive calls.
[04:31] Tomás: for private VPC we'd like HSM support in EU region. is that available?
[04:36] Ethan: we support KMS and can integrate with customer HSMs for private deployments; on-prem package can use local HSM. we'll include more specifics in the security packet.
[04:49] Sara: competitive question: BigCloudAI offered cheaper per-token but no KV cache and their batching was much more aggressive which increased tail latency.
[04:58] Maya: yep, latency tradeoffs are common. our routing and fallback policies aim to keep your SLOs intact even when falling back.
[05:06] Leah: for budgeting: we're comfortable with a pilot up to $8k to validate the numbers. after that procurement needs a forecast.
[05:14] Maya: great. proposed pilot: 2 weeks, three scenarios — hosted baseline, dedicated small reserved pool with burst, and private VPC with quantized model on customer infra (we'll model ops effort). Redwood will run per-token sims and provide expected unit cost and p95 latency.
[05:33] Tomás: what's involved in instrumentation? we need token-level traces and cost breakdowns.
[05:38] Ethan: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost traces, per-route breakdowns, and KV cache hit/miss metrics. we can provide a lightweight SDK wrapper for instrumentation during the pilot.
[05:50] Sara: that'll help. also, curious about failure modes — if reserved pool is saturated, can we fallback gracefully?
[05:56] Maya: yes, automated fallback to hosted model variants or cheaper model classes; you can set policies like prefer-dedicated then hosted then degrade-model. we'll show examples.
[06:07] Leah: from a finance perspective, include a clear cap option so we don't exceed pilot spend.
[06:12] Maya: absolutely — we'll include budget caps and alerting thresholds.
[06:16] Ethan: quick technical note: for your token lengths, typical per-call token total ~550 tokens. with caching and batching we estimate 20-35% per-token reduction in compute in our mid scenario. worst-case (no cache reuse, low batching) you get little benefit.
[06:33] Tomás: any examples of customers with similar footprint?
[06:36] Maya: yes — a retail search customer had similar prompt/response sizes and moved to dedicated+burst; they reduced unit cost ~28% and kept p95 latency ~370ms.
[06:47] Sara: okay good. on data residency, we need EU-only processing for a subset of customers; can we route by region?
[06:53] Ethan: yes, Smart routing supports geo-region policies, plus tenant-level constraints. for private VPC you host in your region.
[07:02] Leah: what's the timeline to get the pilot started?
[07:05] Maya: we can kick off next week, 12/17, with an initial config and instrumentation tasks; Ethan will run sims and we'll deliver a pricing sheet within 3 business days of kickoff.
[07:16] Sara: sounds good. one thing — our ops team prefers minimal agent installs; can Redwood do an agentless instrumentation?
[07:22] Ethan: yes, we provide HTTP middleware & SDK wrappers and can do agentless via sidecarless tracing; for deep metrics we may request a small collector but it's optional.
[07:34] Tomás: one last question: for on-prem quantized model maintenance — who upgrades models and handles drift?
[07:40] Maya: for private deployments we offer a managed option where Redwood can handle model upgrades, or you can self-manage. that will be spelled out in the pilot SOW.
[07:49] Leah: perfect. thanks everyone.
[07:52] Maya: recap of next steps: we'll send pricing spreadsheet, SOC2 & KMS notes, and pilot SOW. Ethan will build the per-token scenarios. Sara/Tomás will send traffic samples and constraints. Leah will confirm budget. schedule kickoff 12/17.
[08:10] Sara: thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript. Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings (Tomás sometimes labeled as Tomas), filler words present, and some technical terms spelled out phonetically (K V cache / kay vee cache).
